nodes.label: Post-Build Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Continues the build plan's stage numbering and rules, dropping only rule 1 so styling is in scope. Covers what remains after Stage 14: a correct, tested, well-secured engine with no bodywork.

nodes.label: Stage 15 — Decisions Before Code
nodes.rationale: Not an engineering task, and it gates the most work per hour of anything in the plan. Q1, Q6 and Q5 actively block Stages 16, 18 and 19; Q11 changes the shape of everything after Stage 17.

nodes.label: Stage 16 — QR Rendering and Camera Scanning
nodes.rationale: react-qr-code for pure SVG rendering at error-correction level M (not H, which adds ~30% more modules and makes each smaller on a phone screen), minimum 240px with a four-module quiet zone on pure white. @zxing/browser for scanning because BarcodeDetector is unavailable in Safari and counter devices are very often iPads.

nodes.label: Stage 17 — Design System and Styling
nodes.rationale: Lower-risk than it sounds because the wireframe annotations were followed literally: this is styling a known thing, not designing an unknown one. The three apps share tokens and primitives but not layout. Accessibility already present (real buttons, associated labels, role=alert, aria-current) must not regress.

nodes.label: Stage 18 — Passcode Delivery
nodes.rationale: No member can sign in without this stage. Build behind a single SmsSender interface so swapping provider later is one file, which matters because the decision may be made on price after a month of real traffic. Qatar specifics with lead times: alphanumeric sender ID registration, delivery to +974 and roaming numbers, and UCS-2 halving the Arabic segment budget.

nodes.label: Stage 19 — Staff MFA
nodes.rationale: TOTP via otplib rather than an SMS second factor, which would depend on Stage 18's provider and is the weakest common second factor. Enrollment shows an otpauth:// QR, which reuses Stage 16's renderer — so Stage 16 must come first. Enrollment is forced on first login because 'without exception' means the un-enrolled state cannot reach anything.

nodes.label: Stage 20 — Hardening for a Public Network
nodes.rationale: The five deferred security-review items: security headers and CORS, httpOnly cookies and CSRF, secret management, edge rate limiting, and alerting. Everything built so far assumed localhost. Give the JWT secret a kid now, even with one key, so rotation later does not need a flag day.

nodes.label: Stage 21 — Deployment
nodes.rationale: Host in Qatar because the membership list is a record of named, prominent individuals and their movements; in-region hosting removes a whole class of cross-border transfer argument before anyone has it. One VM, Docker Compose, Caddy in front — for a programme whose reference card is number three, orchestration is a liability.

nodes.label: Stage 22 — Arabic and RTL
nodes.rationale: The item most likely to be underestimated. The UI half is cheap because Stage 17 used logical properties throughout, but benefit content lives in single-language database columns and needs a translation table. Also decide Arabic-Indic vs Western numerals, Gregorian vs Hijri dates, and which language message templates use.

nodes.label: Stage 23 — App Stores, Install, Push and Wallet
nodes.rationale: Play accepts a Trusted Web Activity wrapping the existing PWA; Apple does not accept PWAs at all and guideline 4.2 rejects repackaged websites. Install without a store is already built with vite-plugin-pwa. The identity payload is NetworkOnly because a cached credential fails at a spa reception with no useful error; benefits and profile are NetworkFirst so R14 still holds.

nodes.label: Stage 24 — Pre-Launch, Non-Engineering
nodes.rationale: DPIA, privacy policy and terms content, consent wording version 1, staff training, a data retention policy that has no answer in code yet, a restore drill run by someone other than the author, and a narrow pilot — one outlet, ten members, four weeks.

nodes.label: Stage 26 — Hotel-Facing Google Sheets Mirror
nodes.rationale: Five managed tabs — _Sync, Members, Benefits, Outlets, Redemptions — rebuilt in full every five minutes. Requests are deliberately absent in v1 because free-text notes and live state do not belong in a standing bulk export. Code acceptance is complete; operational acceptance (hotel approval, data residency, workbook sharing, secret storage) is not.

nodes.label: Stage 27 — Administrator-Only Hotel Access
nodes.rationale: Client-confirmed correction: keep the member guest app and administrator panel, retire every other staff role and surface. Migration 20260809210000_administrator_only_accounts suspends legacy rows and revokes their sessions without deleting or relabelling historical redemption attribution.

nodes.label: Stage 28 — Outlet Fulfilment
nodes.rationale: Partly reverses Stage 27: apps/web-outlet exists, so there are three applications again, though ADMINISTRATOR remains the only account a named person holds. Did not do: the camera on real counter hardware (needs TLS), and a printable card back — the largest remaining gap in the feature as the client described it.

nodes.label: Three Audiences, One API Process
nodes.rationale: The instinct to put the backend on an intranet cannot work: every member screen is an API call and an API reachable only from hotel wifi is an app that only works while standing in the lobby. What can be restricted is which routes are reachable from where, done at the reverse proxy by hostname and source address. The database is never published, on any address.

nodes.label: Three Ordering Constraints
nodes.rationale: Stage 15 before 16 (a different Q1 answer wastes the scanner work); Stage 16 before 19 (MFA enrollment needs the QR renderer); Stage 21 partly before finishing 16 (camera access needs a secure context, so deploy early and unfinished rather than late and complete). Stage 17 is the one genuinely parallelisable split.

nodes.label: BenefitTranslation Table for Arabic Content
nodes.rationale: Adding titleAr/termsAr columns is simpler but bakes 'two languages, forever' into the schema. A table keyed by benefit and locale makes a third language a row rather than a migration. Either way R14 still applies: an administrator changing Arabic terms must not need a deployment.
